incident-bot: PAGER: Dedicated pool - tenant quality regression detected for ACME Corp (acme-vpc-01). Severity: P2. Degraded generation quality after 2026-03-15T09:02Z rollout of quantization profile v2.2. Paging oncall.

Sam (oncall-sre): on it. I see spikes in rerank/errors and a small but consistent semantic drift in outputs for ACME's baseline prompt set. Routing shows ACME pinned to dedicated-pool-4, model redwood-xl-1q (quantized, profile=v2.2). Can someone confirm recent deploys?

Priya (eng-runtime): that deploy was an automated profile rollout we pushed to reduce token cost in dedicated pools. It targeted q-profiles v2.* for all 1q variants. We rolled to 4/6 pools at 09:00Z and included a target mapping rule for dedicated-pool-4.

Jasper (eng-ml): we saw a slight ppl change in internal evals but nothing flagged as regression. However ACME's evaluation prompts include specific instruction-following edge cases — those can be sensitive to quantization changes. Are failures reproducible with ACME prompt set locally?

Sam (oncall-sre): reproducing now. Quick log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T09:04:21Z GET /generate tenant=acme-vpc-01 model=redwood-xl-1q profile=v2.2
prediction: "...irrelevant repetition..."
BLEU/ROUGE drop vs baseline: -12% / -9%
```
Not catastrophic but customer SLA for fidelity is being breached for a subset of requests.

Anika (product): ACME's CS escalation says "severe drop in answer relevance" for support flows. They flagged two active customers impacted. We need to give them an ETA and rollback plan.

Priya (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations we can do:
- Toggle per-tenant model mapping to pin ACME to redwood-xl-1 (fp16, unquantized) on dedicated-pool-4 (fastest, least risk)
- If GPU resources constrained, route ACME to a compatible non-quantized variant in a different pool temporarily
- As a last resort enable model-level soft-fallback to a higher-precision variant for ACME only

Command to pin mapping (run by infra/admin):
```
/redwoodctl routing set-tenant-mapping --tenant acme-vpc-01 --pool dedicated-pool-4 --model redwood-xl-1 --reason "rollback qprofile v2.2 for ACME quality regression"
```

Sam (oncall-sre): I can apply the mapping now if infra approves. Expected cutover ~30s-2min for new requests; KV prefix cache may still return some quantized responses for in-flight sessions.

Jasper (eng-ml): while Sam does that, we'll capture a focused eval of ACME prompt set vs redwood-xl-1q(v2.2) and redwood-xl-1(fp16). If delta is confirmed, we'll propose removing v2.2 from the candidate set for dedicated pools until fixes are in.

CustomerOps - ACME: we appreciate the quick response. Please keep us updated. Priority: customer-facing support flows. We can divert non-critical workloads.

incident-bot: action required: oncall acknowledged. Escalation window: 30m before paging ENG-MLOPS.

Sam (oncall-sre): executing mapping command now (asking infra for RBAC approval). Copying commands I will run:
```
# preview
/redwoodctl routing preview-set --tenant acme-vpc-01 --model redwood-xl-1
# apply
/redwoodctl routing apply --tenant acme-vpc-01 --model redwood-xl-1 --pool dedicated-pool-4
```

Priya (eng-runtime): FYI after apply you'll want to flush per-tenant KV cache for ACME sessions to avoid stale prefix influence:
```
/redwoodctl cache flush --tenant acme-vpc-01 --scope kvprefix
```
Be careful: flush will increase cold-start token cost briefly.

Sam (oncall-sre): mapping applied at 09:14Z. Flushed KV prefix cache. Observing first 10 requests — qualitatively looks better. Latency unchanged. Monitoring evaluations running.

Jasper (eng-ml): early eval post-rollback: BLEU/ROUGE back within 1-2% of baseline. Looks like quantization profile v2.2 is the likely culprit for ACME's prompt distribution.

Anika (product): messaging to ACME: "We've rolled ACME back to the previous model variant and are monitoring. Initial checks show relevance restored. We'll follow up with root-cause and timeline for a permanent fix." Can someone draft short note for CS?

CustomerOps - ACME: confirmed better on our end. Thanks — we'll keep an eye and reopen if we see issues.

Priya (eng-runtime): next steps:
- Block v2.2 rollout to dedicated-pool-4 until ML approves
- ML to run targeted regression tests on tenant-specific prompt sets before future q-profile rollouts
- Create a temporary canary policy to run q-profile changes on 1% traffic with tenant-aware exclusions

Jasper (eng-ml): Agreed. I'll roll the v2.2 candidate back from dedicated-pool-4 and run a focused retrain/eval. I'll also add ACME prompt set checks to our pre-rollout gating.

Sam (oncall-sre): Handoff: I'm on till 10:00Z. If ACME still stable at 10:00Z, @Priya will take over monitoring for the rest of the window. Logging summary and commands used attached above.

incident-bot: Note: Incident thread will auto-close if no activity for 60m. Manually tag postmortem if we need one.

Anika (product): Let's schedule a quick post-incident sync with ACME and customer success today. Capture timeline, RCA, and compensation if required.

Sam (oncall-sre): marking incident as mitigated -> tentative. Will update if we see regressions. :thumbsup:
